enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Choose Picture A (the village children around a toddler holding a tablet) and say so.
2. Introduction: describe the picture in two sentences and link it to a memory.
3. The arrival of the tablet in the village and the excitement of the children.
4. What the children learnt and the problem that followed (neglecting the farm work).
5. The grandfather's solution and a conclusion on technology used with discipline.

**Model composition (466 words)**

Picture A shows a group of village children crowded around a toddler who is holding a tablet. The little boy looks at the screen with delight, while the older children smile, laugh and press their hands to their mouths in excitement. This picture reminds me of the day a tablet reached my grandfather's village and changed the lives of the children.

It was during the Christmas holidays when my cousin Ayuk came from Douala with a tablet that his father had bought for him. In my grandfather's village, nobody had ever seen such a thing. News of the strange gadget spread like wildfire, and by the afternoon, a crowd of children had gathered under the big tree in front of our compound.

Ayuk sat on a stool and touched the screen. Pictures of animals, cartoons and songs appeared, and the children gasped. A small boy named Neba, who was only three, pushed through the crowd and begged to hold it. Ayuk hesitated, but he finally let him. Neba held the tablet with both hands and stared, laughing with joy, while the rest of us leaned over his shoulders. I remember how the toddler's mother stood behind us, smiling with pride at her little boy, who was learning faster than all of us. One boy covered his mouth with his hands, and another was so surprised that his mouth hung open.

That day we learnt many things from that screen. Ayuk showed us a video about the sea, which none of us had seen, and a lesson that taught the alphabet and counting. The younger children tried to repeat the letters, and the older ones asked questions about distant countries. For the first time, I felt that the whole world could come to our little village.

In the following days, however, a problem appeared. Some children refused to help their parents on the farm, because they wanted to spend the whole day in front of the tablet. My grandfather, who is a wise man, called us together and said, "A tool is good only if you use it well. The screen can teach you, but it cannot plant your cassava or fetch your water." He then arranged a timetable: one hour of learning every evening after the farm work.

The plan worked. The children learnt new words, drew pictures and even taught the adults how to send a message. The village women, who had never gone to school, also came in the evenings to watch and learn, and soon the whole compound became a small classroom. Many years later, Neba became the first person from our village to study computer science at university.

The picture reminds me that technology is a wonderful gift when it is used with discipline, and that curiosity is the beginning of knowledge.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. No clear link with the picture chosen, or not saying which picture is used.
2. Describing the picture line by line instead of building a story or a composition from it.
